questions.question: A sealed container holds $n = 2\ \mathrm{mol}$ of an ideal gas at $T = 300\ \mathrm{K}$ and $P = 1.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$. Find the volume $V$. Use $R = 8.31\ \mathrm{J/(mol\cdot K)}$.
A fixed-volume container holds an ideal gas at $P_1 = 1.2\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ and $T_1 = 300\ \mathrm{K}$. The gas is heated to $T_2 = 450\ \mathrm{K}$. Find the new pressure $P_2$.

A gas occupies $V_1 = 4\ \mathrm{L}$ at $T_1 = 27^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $P_1 = 1\ \mathrm{atm}$. It is compressed to $V_2 = 1\ \mathrm{L}$ while the temperature is raised to $T_2 = 127^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Find the final pressure $P_2$.
questions.answer:
Convert temperatures to Kelvin: $T_1 = 300\ \mathrm{K}$, $T_2 = 400\ \mathrm{K}$.

Combined gas law: $\dfrac{P_1 V_1}{T_1} = \dfrac{P_2 V_2}{T_2}$

$P_2 = P_1 \cdot \dfrac{V_1}{V_2} \cdot \dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = 1 \times \dfrac{4}{1} \times \dfrac{400}{300} = \dfrac{16}{3} \approx 5.33\ \mathrm{atm}$

questions.question: At standard conditions ($T = 273\ \mathrm{K}$, $P = 1.013\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$), $1\ \mathrm{mol}$ of an ideal gas occupies $22.4\ \mathrm{L}$. Verify this using $R = 8.31\ \mathrm{J/(mol\cdot K)}$.
questions.answer:
$V = \dfrac{nRT}{P} = \dfrac{1 \times 8.31 \times 273}{1.013\times10^5} = \dfrac{2268.6}{1.013\times10^5} = 0.02239\ \mathrm{m^3}$

$= 22.39\ \mathrm{L} \approx 22.4\ \mathrm{L}$ ✓

This is the standard molar volume of an ideal gas at STP.

questions.question: A cylinder contains $n = 0.5\ \mathrm{mol}$ of ideal gas at $T = 400\ \mathrm{K}$. The piston maintains constant pressure $P = 2.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$. The gas cools to $T' = 200\ \mathrm{K}$. Find: (a) the initial and final volumes, (b) the work done by the gas.
questions.answer:
**(a)** $V = nRT/P$

$V_1 = \dfrac{0.5 \times 8.31 \times 400}{2.0\times10^5} = \dfrac{1662}{2\times10^5} = 8.31\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^3}$

$V_2 = \dfrac{0.5 \times 8.31 \times 200}{2.0\times10^5} = \dfrac{831}{2\times10^5} = 4.155\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^3}$

**(b)** Work done by gas at constant pressure:

$W = P(V_2 - V_1) = 2.0\times10^5 \times (4.155 - 8.31)\times10^{-3} = 2.0\times10^5 \times (-4.155\times10^{-3})$

$W = -831\ \mathrm{J}$

(Negative: gas is compressed, work is done **on** the gas.)

questions.question: A weather balloon contains helium at $T = 20^\circ\mathrm{C}$, $P = 1.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$, $V = 1.0\ \mathrm{m^3}$. At altitude, $P$ drops to $0.4\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ and $T$ drops to $-20^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Find the new volume.
questions.answer:
$T_1 = 293\ \mathrm{K}$, $T_2 = 253\ \mathrm{K}$

$V_2 = V_1 \cdot \dfrac{P_1}{P_2} \cdot \dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = 1.0 \times \dfrac{1.0\times10^5}{0.4\times10^5} \times \dfrac{253}{293}$

$= 2.5 \times 0.864 = 2.16\ \mathrm{m^3}$

The balloon expands to 2.16 times its original volume.

questions.question: A room has dimensions $5\ \mathrm{m} \times 4\ \mathrm{m} \times 3\ \mathrm{m}$ and contains air at $P = 1.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ and $T = 300\ \mathrm{K}$. Find the number of moles of air in the room. Use $R = 8.31\ \mathrm{J/(mol\cdot K)}$.
questions.answer:
$V = 5 \times 4 \times 3 = 60\ \mathrm{m^3}$

$n = \dfrac{PV}{RT} = \dfrac{1.0\times10^5 \times 60}{8.31 \times 300} = \dfrac{6.0\times10^6}{2493} \approx 2406\ \mathrm{mol}$

With molar mass of air $\approx 29\ \mathrm{g/mol}$: mass $\approx 2406 \times 0.029 \approx 69.8\ \mathrm{kg}$

questions.question: A gas is enclosed in a container of fixed volume. When the temperature is $T_1 = 17^\circ\mathrm{C}$, the pressure is $P_1 = 1.2\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$. At what temperature (in $^\circ\mathrm{C}$) will the pressure be $P_2 = 1.6\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$?

A gas occupies $V_1 = 10\ \mathrm{L}$ at $T = 300\ \mathrm{K}$. It is compressed isothermally until $V_2 = 2\ \mathrm{L}$. By what factor does the pressure change? If the original pressure was $P_1 = 1.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$, find $P_2$.
questions.answer:
Isothermal process: $P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2$

$\dfrac{P_2}{P_1} = \dfrac{V_1}{V_2} = \dfrac{10}{2} = 5$

$P_2 = 5 \times 1.0\times10^5 = 5.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

Compressing to 1/5 the volume multiplies pressure by 5.

questions.question: A container is divided into two equal compartments by a removable partition. The left side holds gas A: $n_A = 2\ \mathrm{mol}$, $T = 300\ \mathrm{K}$. The right side holds gas B: $n_B = 3\ \mathrm{mol}$, $T = 300\ \mathrm{K}$. Both sides have the same volume $V_0$. When the partition is removed, find the final pressure (assume $T$ stays at $300\ \mathrm{K}$).
questions.answer:
Initial pressures:

$P_A = \dfrac{n_A RT}{V_0}$, $P_B = \dfrac{n_B RT}{V_0}$

After mixing: total moles $= n_A + n_B = 5$, total volume $= 2V_0$, temperature unchanged.

$P_f = \dfrac{(n_A + n_B)RT}{2V_0} = \dfrac{5RT}{2V_0}$

Compare to initial: $P_A = 2RT/V_0$, $P_B = 3RT/V_0$

$P_f = \dfrac{5RT}{2V_0} = 2.5 \dfrac{RT}{V_0}$

This equals the average of the partial pressures: $\frac{P_A + P_B}{2} = \frac{2+3}{2}\dfrac{RT}{V_0} = 2.5\dfrac{RT}{V_0}$ ✓
